'''Umpithamu''', also spelt '''Umbindhamu''', is an [[Australian Aboriginal language]] of the [[Cape York Peninsula]], [[Queensland]], Australia.

==Classification==
Though generally accepted as a branch of the [[Paman languages]], Dixon believes it to be an [[language isolate|isolate]]. According to Rigsby (1997), Umpithamu shares some grammatical features with the other languages spoken by the Lamalama people, but it shares more lexicon with [[Ayapathu language|Ayapathu]] and [[Umpila language|Umpila]].<ref name="AIATSIS" />

In 2008, Verstraete wrote that there were four languages associated with the [[Lamalama people]]: Umpithamu, [[Morrobolam language|Morrobolam]], [[Mba Rumbathama]] (Mbarrumbathama, Lamalama) and [[Rimanggudinhma language]] (Mbariman-Gudhinma).<ref name="AIATSIS" /> In 2020, he spoke of five languages associated with the Lamalama people, but the name of the fifth is not recorded in the article.<ref name="rigby" />

He is quoted by [[Austlang]] from his 2018 work, ''The Genetic Status of Lamalamic'', that Lamalama, Rimanggudinhma and Morrobolam form a [[Genetic relationship (linguistics)|genetic]] subgroup of Paman known as Lamalamic, "defined by shared innovations in phonology and morphology".<ref>{{cite web | title=Y55: Morrobolam | website=AIATSIS Collection (Austlang) | date=26 July 2019 | url=https://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/Y55 | access-date=7 August 2020}}</ref>

"Yintjinggu/Jintjingga" is a place name used for both Umpithamu and the neighbouring [[Ayabadhu language]].<ref name="AIATSIS" /><ref name="austlangY60">{{cite web |title=Y60: Ayapathu |url=https://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/Y60 |access-date=3 June 2022 |website=Australian Indigenous Languages Database |date=26 July 2019 |publisher=[[Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies]]}}</ref>

== Documentation ==
In July 2020, ''A Dictionary of Umpithamu'' was published, compiled by [[Flemish people|Flemish]] linguist Jean-Christophe Verstraete, with main language consultants Florrie Bassani and her niece Joan Liddy.<ref name=rigby>{{cite web | title=First Cape York Indigenous language dictionary in 20 years published by Flemish linguist |first=Mark|last=Rigby| website=ABC News|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation | date=5 August 2020 | url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-08-06/dictionary-of-unique-cape-york-indigenous-language-published/12525128 | access-date=7 August 2020}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite book | title=A dictionary of Umpithamu: With notes on Middle Paman | publisher=Aboriginal Studies Press|first=Jean-Christophe|last= Verstraete | date=2020 |isbn=9781925302219 }}</ref>
